working_title: County Down's Golf Circuit: A Practical Guide to Playing Royal County Down, Ardglass and Kirkistown Castle
angle: County Down is home to one of the world's great links in Royal County Down, but the county has a broader golf circuit that UK visitors often overlook. This post treats it as a practical itinerary: how to actually get there from the mainland, what Royal County Down demands of a visitor, and which supporting courses (Ardglass, Kirkistown Castle, Clandeboye) make a multi-day trip worth building around.
research_notes:
- Royal County Down (RCD), Newcastle, County Down. Founded 1889. Designed originally by Old Tom Morris, refined by Harry Colt. Championship Links: par 71, 7,186 yards. Annesley Links (second course): par 66, 4,548 yards. Both open to visitors.
- RCD visitor days: all day Monday, Tuesday, Friday; Thursday mornings; Sunday afternoons. No visitors Wednesdays or Saturdays. Advance booking essential; availability is limited.
- RCD Championship green fees listed at £425 for 2025 (one source notes an 18% rise to £425 for 2025); Annesley Links considerably cheaper (one source: around £19–£30 midweek). Do NOT quote a specific Championship fee as confirmed current — describe as 'premium' and direct readers to the club directly.
- Slope rating 142 (Championship). Multiple blind tee shots — a caddie is widely recommended, especially for first-timers.
- Course set in Murlough Nature Reserve between Mourne Mountains and Irish Sea/Dundrum Bay. The ninth hole described as one of the most photographed holes in world golf.
- Ardglass Golf Club: 18-hole clifftop links, Ardglass village, County Down. Founded 1896. Par 70, approximately 6,268 yards from medal tees. Visitors welcome. About 30 minutes from RCD at Newcastle; under an hour from Belfast. Clubhouse occupies a fortified building dating to around 1405 AD — one of the oldest golf clubhouses in the world. Sea views from every hole; Irish Sea comes into play on multiple holes. Regularly paired with RCD as part of a County Down circuit.
- Kirkistown Castle Golf Club: Cloughey, Ards Peninsula, County Down. Links course, 18 holes. Redesigned by James Braid in 1934. Visitors welcome 7 days a week. Green fees relatively modest (midweek from approximately £35–£40 range per sources — note figures vary and may have changed; describe as significantly cheaper than RCD rather than quoting a definitive figure). Sandy base means playable year-round. Known as the closest true links to Belfast.
- Clandeboye Golf Club: two courses (Dufferin — heathland/parkland, par 71, 6,742 yards championship; Ava — shorter). Located near Bangor/Newtownards. Midweek guide fees approximately £40 (Dufferin) and £35 (Ava) per Golfshake — treat as indicative, verify with club. Visitors welcome chiefly on weekdays.
- Getting there from mainland UK: Cairnryan (Scotland) to Belfast ferry (Stena Line/P&O) around 2h15m crossing. Liverpool (Birkenhead) to Belfast ferry also available (~8 hours overnight). Flying into Belfast International or George Best Belfast City also options. Newcastle (RCD) is roughly 30–45 minutes south of Belfast via the A24. Ardglass approximately 30 minutes further along the coast from Newcastle. Kirkistown Castle is on the Ards Peninsula, around an hour north of Newcastle.
- Slieve Donard Resort and Spa (five-star hotel) is immediately adjacent to RCD — well-known base for golf trips in the area. Mention informationally only; do not add affiliate link unless pre-approved.
- A handicap certificate or proof of handicap is required to play RCD Championship Links.
- No buggy hire at RCD; trolleys available; club hire available subject to availability.
